svg.title: Compare transcript forms without changing the inherited genome
svg.desc: A simplified primary RNA transcript contains exon1,intron,exon2,intron,exon3. Two possible mature transcript forms retain1-2-3 and1-3 respectively; matching exon colours and numbers remain in order. Introns are removed in processing and exon2 can be omitted in this illustrative alternative-splicing model. Exons are retained regions and may include untranslated sequence; not every exon base codes for amino acid. Cap and poly-A details are omitted rather than denied. Shared inherited DNA does not imply identical transcript form or abundance across tissues. Protein accumulation also depends on translation and degradation, so abundant RNA alone does not identify the cause of a low protein amount.

g.text: Compare transcript forms without changing the inherited genome
An exact block map distinguishes retained regions, processing and later protein evidence.
One simplified primary transcript: retained exons plus removable introns
Illustrative alternative splicing retains exons 1 and 3 in both forms; exon 2 differs.
Not every exon nucleotide must encode an amino acid. End modifications are omitted from this map.
DNA presence → transcript form/amount → translation → protein stability/function need separate evidence.
Abundant mRNA with little protein can reflect slow translation or rapid protein breakdown.
